note: One row per attempt. Official time runs from the player's first spawn to the [Free the End] advancement in the server log. Run records are private except the excerpts in records/. tools/make_readme.py writes the README's paper list from this file.
category: One LLM agent in one continuous session, playing Minecraft Java 1.20.4 survival on Easy in an unfiltered random world, through programs it sends to a Mineflayer bot (the setup of Faldor et al. 2026, arXiv 2610.22319)

record.claim: Fastest in the category to our knowledge; no organisation keeps this record

reference.name: Faldor et al. (2026), four Gemini 4 Argon agents

runs.caveats: One run on one world. The agent had the Gemini team's paper and guides drawn from it, which that team did not have.
One run on a new world, so the speed-up over run 1 mixes the inherited files, the higher effort, the owner's rules and the luck of the world.

runs.official_time: no win, ended by the owner at 10:58:17
runs.seed: random, given in the run 4 paper
runs.caveats: No paper of its own; described in the run 4 paper.
It missed its own 5-hour plan by 1 h 51 min. The record until run 5.

runs.players: 2 agents and 2 humans playing by hand
runs.deaths: 7 by the agents, 31 by the humans
runs.caveats: Outside the category: a human made the winning hit, and the humans did at least 34.9% of the dragon's damage, partly with beds. Its clock starts at the first agent's spawn.

runs.players: 2 agents, each alone on its own copy of one world
runs.official_time: no win, both stopped at 5:17 by a usage limit
runs.seed: one random seed shared by both arms, withheld
runs.caveats: No win, one pair, and a shared seed. The subscription's usage limit ended it, not the game.
One run on one world, 20 minutes inside its 5-hour plan. The paper's author is the agent that wrote the plan. The 73% repeat estimate should be read with the paper's cautions.

runs.players: 2 agents and 2 humans playing by hand
runs.deaths: 1 by the agents, 7 by the humans
runs.caveats: Outside the category: the humans took about 98% of the dragon's health after the crystals, by hand with swords and an axe (no beds), and a human made the winning hit. The same two humans had played the first team run and a rehearsal that evening. Its clock starts at the first agent's spawn.

runs.model: Claude Fable 5.2 as the planning agent (the player it planned for is Run 5's)
runs.players: no run of its own: 1 human and 1 planning agent in one conversation
runs.official_time: no run of its own; a study of the planning conversation behind Run 5
runs.caveats: One conversation and one run, with names given four days later. The rise in the plan's chances is the planning agent's own estimate; no run played an earlier edit of the plan. The claim that Fable 5.2 forecasts tasks better than earlier models is the human's impression, and the paper's use as context for future agents is untested.
